memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "And the Lord did this. Dense swarms of flies poured into Pharaoh's palace and into the houses of his officials; throughout Egypt the land was ruined by the flies." - Exodus 8:24 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The land was ruined. Not inconvenienced — ruined.

We should not read the plagues as entertainment. Real people suffered. Ordinary Egyptian families, who had never made a policy decision in their lives, watched their homes and livelihoods destroyed because their ruler would not yield.

That is the true cost of stubborn leadership. Pharaoh's pride ruined a nation. The people who suffered most were those with the least power.

It should make us examine our own influence. Parents, managers, teachers, church leaders, older siblings — our decisions land on people who did not make them. Refusing to apologise, refusing to change, refusing to listen: these are not private choices when others depend on us.

Jesus turned the world's model of leadership upside down, saying that whoever wants to be great must be a servant (Mk 10:43-44). Servant leaders absorb cost rather than passing it down.

Whatever authority God has given you, use it to shelter people, not to spend them.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Who bears the cost when I refuse to change or admit fault?
2. Am I using my influence to serve or to protect my own position?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, make me a leader who serves. Do not let my pride cost the people entrusted to me. Amen.
